subject: English
title: Arjun and Priya Learn the Magic Words
hook: Every word in English has a special job. Meet Arjun and Priya as they discover the eight magic word types!

slides.title: Arjun and Priya Learn the Magic Words
Arjun's Word Discovery
slides.storyContext: Arjun finds a mysterious book that labels every word. He calls his friend Priya to help decode it.
slides.inSimpleWords: Every word has a job in English.

image.alt: Arjun's Word Discovery — Parts of Speech

slides.title: What Are Parts of Speech?
slides.storyContext: Priya explains: 'Every word in English does one of eight jobs. Like a team with different players!'

points.label: Parts of speech
points.text: Eight word types: each has a special job in sentences

points.label: Why learn them?
points.text: Understand how words work together to build meaning

slides.inSimpleWords: Eight word types build all English sentences.

slides.title: Nouns: The Name Givers
slides.storyContext: Priya points: 'These words name things.' They spot dog, school, happiness, Arjun.

points.label: What is a noun?
points.text: A word that names a person, place, thing, or idea

points.label: Examples
points.text: Teacher, Delhi, book, courage

slides.inSimpleWords: Nouns name people, places, things, feelings.

image.alt: Nouns: The Name Givers — Parts of Speech

slides.title: Nouns in Sentences
slides.storyContext: Arjun reads: 'The teacher in Delhi loves books. The student shows courage.' Find each noun!

example.problem: Identify all nouns in: 'The girl ran to school with her friend.'
example.solution: Nouns: girl, school, friend. (The, ran, to, with are other parts of speech.)

slides.inSimpleWords: Nouns are the main 'things' in sentences.

slides.title: Verbs: The Action Words
slides.storyContext: Arjun jumps. Priya runs. Their action book glows brightly. 'These are verbs!' Arjun shouts.

points.label: What is a verb?
points.text: A word that shows action or state of being

points.label: Examples
points.text: Run, sing, sleep, think, is, become

slides.inSimpleWords: Verbs show what someone is doing.

image.alt: Verbs: The Action Words — Parts of Speech

slides.title: Verbs in Sentences
slides.storyContext: Priya lists: 'Arjun runs fast. I sing songs. She is happy. The book became famous.' All are verbs!

example.problem: What verb shows action in: 'The boy eats mango under the tree'?
example.solution: Verb: eats. (The, boy, mango, under, tree are not verbs.)

slides.inSimpleWords: Verbs are the 'doing' words in sentences.

slides.title: Adjectives: The Describers
slides.storyContext: The book is old. It has beautiful pages and mysterious words. Priya laughs: 'These paint pictures!'

points.label: What is an adjective?
points.text: A word that describes a noun

points.label: Examples
points.text: Happy, blue, small, brilliant, soft

slides.inSimpleWords: Adjectives describe how things look.

image.alt: Adjectives: The Describers — Parts of Speech

slides.title: Adjectives in Sentences
slides.storyContext: Arjun says: 'The red car is fast. Priya wore a beautiful dress. This small pen is old.' Adjectives add color!

example.problem: Find adjectives in: 'The young boy wore a blue shirt and new shoes.'
example.solution: Adjectives: young, blue, new. (They describe the nouns boy, shirt, shoes.)

slides.inSimpleWords: Adjectives make descriptions richer.

slides.title: Adverbs: The Detail Givers
slides.storyContext: They read slowly. The words appear suddenly. Everything happens quickly. 'Adverbs tell HOW!' Priya explains.

points.label: What is an adverb?
points.text: A word that describes a verb, adjective, or another adverb

points.label: Examples
points.text: Quickly, happily, very, slowly, almost

slides.inSimpleWords: Adverbs tell how, when, or where.

image.alt: Adverbs: The Detail Givers — Parts of Speech

slides.title: Adverbs in Sentences
slides.storyContext: Priya reads: 'Arjun ran very quickly. She sang beautifully today. They almost won.' Adverbs modify everything!

example.problem: Spot adverbs in: 'The car moved slowly and carefully across the bridge.'
example.solution: Adverbs: slowly, carefully. (They modify the verb 'moved'.)

slides.inSimpleWords: Adverbs describe actions in detail.

slides.title: Pronouns: The Replacers
slides.storyContext: Arjun says: 'I went to the store. He bought juice. She found books. They played together.' Simple pronouns!

points.label: What is a pronoun?
points.text: A word that replaces a noun (I, you, he, she, it, we, they)

points.label: Examples
points.text: I, me, you, he, she, it, we, us, they, them

slides.inSimpleWords: Pronouns replace noun names.

slides.title: Prepositions: The Connectors
slides.storyContext: Priya draws: 'The book is ON the table. Arjun is IN the class. The pen is UNDER the desk.' Prepositions show position!

points.label: What is a preposition?
points.text: A word that shows the position or relationship between things

points.label: Examples
points.text: In, on, under, above, beside, between, through, across

slides.inSimpleWords: Prepositions show where and how.

slides.title: Conjunctions: The Joiners
slides.storyContext: Arjun writes: 'I like tea AND coffee. She wants to play BUT must study. Come IF you can.' Conjunctions connect!

points.label: What is a conjunction?
points.text: A word that joins words, phrases, or sentences

points.label: Examples
points.text: And, but, or, because, if, while, since, until

slides.inSimpleWords: Conjunctions join ideas together.

slides.title: Interjections: The Exclamers
slides.storyContext: Arjun shouts: 'Wow! Amazing! Ouch! Help! Oh my! Hurray!' Priya nods: 'These show strong feeling!'

points.label: What is an interjection?
points.text: A word that shows emotion or surprise (usually followed by !)

points.label: Examples
points.text: Wow, ouch, hurray, oh, alas, hello, goodbye

slides.inSimpleWords: Interjections show emotion!

slides.title: More Parts of Speech
slides.storyContext: Arjun finds four more types: pronouns (he, she), prepositions (in, under), conjunctions (and, but), and interjections (Wow!).

example.problem: What parts of speech haven't we learned?
example.solution: Pronouns (I, you, they), Prepositions (in, on), Conjunctions (and, or), Interjections (Ouch!)

slides.inSimpleWords: Eight word types work together in sentences.

image.alt: More Parts of Speech — Parts of Speech

slides.title: All Eight Parts Together
slides.storyContext: Priya builds a sentence: 'Wow! The quick brown fox jumped over the fence very carefully.' Let's label every word!

example.problem: Identify ALL parts of speech: 'She quickly ate a delicious apple in the garden.'
example.solution: She (pronoun) quickly (adverb) ate (verb) a (article) delicious (adjective) apple (noun) in (preposition) the (article) garden (noun).

slides.inSimpleWords: Every word belongs to one of eight types.

slides.title: Spot the Parts
slides.storyContext: Arjun points to a sentence: 'The happy child ran quickly to the park.' Can you label each word type?

points.label: Try this
points.text: The (article) happy (adjective) child (noun) ran (verb) quickly (adverb)

slides.inSimpleWords: Identify nouns, verbs, and adjectives easily.

image.alt: Spot the Parts — Parts of Speech

slides.title: Label Every Word
slides.storyContext: Priya gives a challenge: 'Oh! The beautiful garden has many colorful flowers and butterflies that dance gracefully.'

points.label: Challenge
points.text: Label: noun, verb, adjective, adverb, preposition, pronoun, conjunction, interjection

slides.inSimpleWords: Master labeling all eight word types.

slides.title: How to Find Each Part of Speech
slides.storyContext: Priya teaches tricks: Ask 'What?' for nouns. Ask 'What's the action?' for verbs. Ask 'What kind?' for adjectives.

points.label: Noun test
points.text: Ask 'What is this?' → Answer is a noun

points.label: Verb test
points.text: Ask 'What's happening?' → Answer is a verb

points.label: Adjective test
points.text: Ask 'What kind/what color?' → Answer is an adjective

slides.inSimpleWords: Use simple questions to identify parts.

slides.title: Compound Sentences with Mixed Parts
slides.storyContext: Arjun builds: 'While Priya quickly read the red book, I happily ate delicious mango and she danced joyfully!'

example.problem: Parse: 'The tall boy ran very quickly and she happily jumped over the wall.'
example.solution: The (article) tall (adj) boy (noun) ran (verb) very (adverb) quickly (adverb) and (conj) she (pronoun) happily (adverb) jumped (verb) over (prep) the (article) wall (noun).

slides.inSimpleWords: Complex sentences use multiple word types.

slides.title: Build Your Own Sentence
slides.storyContext: Arjun challenges Priya: 'Write a sentence using at least one of each part of speech!'

points.label: Try it
points.text: Example: 'Wow! I quickly ate a delicious mango in the park with my friend and felt happy.'

slides.inSimpleWords: Create sentences using all eight word types.

slides.title: Common Adjective-Noun Pairs
slides.storyContext: Priya lists pairs: 'bright sun, cold water, happy child, soft pillow, tall building.' Adjectives paint vivid pictures!

points.label: Color + noun
points.text: red ball, blue sky, green tree

points.label: Size + noun
points.text: big house, small flower, tiny ant

slides.inSimpleWords: Adjectives make nouns more interesting.

slides.title: Adverbs Modifying Different Things
slides.storyContext: Arjun shows: 'Slowly (modifies verb). Very hot (modifies adjective). Almost always (modifies adverb). Adverbs are flexible!'

example.problem: Identify what adverb modifies: 'She sang very beautifully.'
example.solution: Very modifies beautifully (adverb). Beautifully modifies sang (verb).

slides.inSimpleWords: Adverbs modify verbs, adjectives, or other adverbs.

slides.title: Pronoun Forms: Subject vs Object
slides.storyContext: Priya teaches: 'I play (subject). She knows me (object). He helps us (object). Words change based on their job!'

points.label: Subject pronouns
points.text: I, you, he, she, it, we, they (doing the action)

points.label: Object pronouns
points.text: me, you, him, her, it, us, them (receiving the action)

slides.inSimpleWords: Pronouns change form depending on their role.

slides.title: Prepositions of Time and Place
slides.storyContext: Arjun maps: 'I live IN the city (place). I work AT 9 AM (time). I wait DURING class (time).' Prepositions locate!

example.problem: Fill prepositions: 'She sleeps __ the night. He studies __ 3 PM. They play __ the park.'
example.solution: She sleeps during the night. He studies at 3 PM. They play in the park.

slides.inSimpleWords: Prepositions show time and place.

slides.title: Spot All Word Types in a Paragraph
slides.storyContext: Priya reads: 'Yesterday, my friend and I went to an old library. We found amazing books and read them happily! Oh, how wonderful!'

points.label: Challenge
points.text: Find: nouns, verbs, adjectives, adverbs, pronouns, prepositions, conjunctions, interjections

slides.inSimpleWords: Practice identifying all eight parts in real text.

slides.title: The Book's Final Gift
slides.storyContext: The magical book closes. Arjun and Priya realize they can now build sentences with confidence and power.
slides.inSimpleWords: Understanding parts of speech unlocks English.

image.alt: The Book's Final Gift — Parts of Speech

slides.title: Your Word Powers
slides.storyContext: Eight types: noun, verb, adjective, adverb, pronoun, preposition, conjunction, interjection.
slides.inSimpleWords: Every word has a job. Learn it!

image.alt: Your Word Powers — Parts of Speech

subject: English
title: Arjun and Priya Travel Through Time
hook: Past, present, future. Three time zones to explore with Arjun and Priya!

slides.title: Arjun and Priya Travel Through Time
The Time Machine
slides.storyContext: Arjun and Priya discover a strange device. 'It shows three times,' Priya whispers. 'Past, now, and future!'
slides.inSimpleWords: Verbs change shape in different times.

image.alt: The Time Machine — Tenses

slides.title: What Are Tenses?
slides.storyContext: Priya explains: 'Tenses tell WHEN an action happens. Every verb changes its form based on time.'

points.label: What is a tense?
points.text: The form of a verb that shows when an action happens

points.label: Three main tenses
points.text: Past (finished), Present (happening now), Future (will happen)

slides.inSimpleWords: Tenses tell us WHEN something happens.

slides.title: Past Tense: What Already Happened
slides.storyContext: They look at the screen. 'Yesterday, we walked to school. I ate mango.' Priya explains: these events finished.

points.label: What is past tense?
points.text: Verbs that show actions already completed

points.label: Examples
points.text: walked, played, ate, learned, sang

slides.inSimpleWords: Past tense: actions that already happened.

image.alt: Past Tense: What Already Happened — Tenses

slides.title: Past Tense Examples
slides.storyContext: Arjun lists: 'I walked home. She played cricket. They learned English. The bird flew away.'

example.problem: Change to past tense: 'I eat lunch. She plays games. They sing songs.'
example.solution: I ate lunch. She played games. They sang songs.

slides.inSimpleWords: Most past tense verbs add -ed.

slides.title: Present Tense: What's Happening Now
slides.storyContext: The device shows: 'Right now, I walk. I eat. I am happy.' Arjun says, 'It's happening RIGHT NOW!'

points.label: What is present tense?
points.text: Verbs that show actions happening now

points.label: Examples
points.text: walk, play, eat, learn, am singing

slides.inSimpleWords: Present tense: actions happening now.

image.alt: Present Tense: What's Happening Now — Tenses

slides.title: Present Tense Examples
slides.storyContext: Priya reads: 'I play soccer. He runs fast. We eat rice. The sun shines brightly.'

example.problem: Change to present tense: 'I walked. She played. They learned.'
example.solution: I walk. She plays. They learn.

slides.inSimpleWords: Present tense shows current actions.

slides.title: Future Tense: What Will Happen
slides.storyContext: They see tomorrow's screen: 'Tomorrow, I will walk. I will play cricket. I will be happy.' Future is coming!

points.label: What is future tense?
points.text: Verbs that show actions that will happen

points.label: Examples
points.text: will walk, will play, will eat, will go, will sing

slides.inSimpleWords: Future tense: actions that will happen.

image.alt: Future Tense: What Will Happen — Tenses

slides.title: Future Tense Examples
slides.storyContext: Arjun predicts: 'I will study tomorrow. She will visit her friend. They will play tomorrow.'

example.problem: Change to future tense: 'I walk. She plays. They eat.'
example.solution: I will walk. She will play. They will eat.

slides.inSimpleWords: Future tense adds 'will' before verbs.

slides.title: Three Tenses in One Story
slides.storyContext: Priya tells: 'Yesterday I played (past). Today I play (present). Tomorrow I will play (future).' One action, three tenses!

example.problem: How do I write the same action in three tenses?
example.solution: Past: walked. Present: walk. Future: will walk.

slides.inSimpleWords: Same verb changes with different times.

image.alt: Three Tenses in One Story — Tenses

slides.title: Tense Transformation
slides.storyContext: Arjun writes: 'Drink water (present) → Drank water (past) → Will drink water (future).'

example.problem: Show three tenses of 'run'
example.solution: Ran (past), Run (present), Will run (future)

slides.inSimpleWords: Learn the three forms of each verb.

slides.title: Time Zone Quiz
slides.storyContext: Arjun points to verbs. Is 'ran' past or present? Is 'will jump' future or past? Priya checks each answer.

points.label: Spot it
points.text: ran (past), jumps (present), will run (future)

slides.inSimpleWords: Learn to spot past, present, future.

image.alt: Time Zone Quiz — Tenses

slides.title: Sort by Time
slides.storyContext: Priya mixes verbs: 'jumped, walks, will sing, played, eats, will run.' Sort them into past, present, future!

points.label: Try this
points.text: Past: jumped, played. Present: walks, eats. Future: will sing, will run.

slides.inSimpleWords: Identify tenses by their form.

slides.title: Irregular Verbs: The Tricksters
slides.storyContext: Arjun discovers some verbs don't follow the -ed rule. 'Go → went. Eat → ate. See → saw. These are special!'

points.label: Irregular verbs
points.text: Don't add -ed; they change completely in past tense

points.label: Examples
points.text: go/went, eat/ate, see/saw, run/ran, swim/swam, sit/sat, come/came

slides.inSimpleWords: Some verbs change in unpredictable ways.

slides.title: Irregular Verbs in Sentences
slides.storyContext: Priya writes: 'Yesterday I went to school. I ate lunch. I saw my friend. I sat and talked with her.'

example.problem: Change these irregular verbs to past: 'I run fast. I eat rice. I come early.'
example.solution: I ran fast. I ate rice. I came early.

slides.inSimpleWords: Learn common irregular verb forms.

slides.title: Using Tenses in Stories
slides.storyContext: Arjun realizes: 'Stories use past tense. Instructions use present. Plans use future. Each tells differently!'

points.label: Past for stories
points.text: She walked to school and bought a book.

points.label: Present for now
points.text: She walks to school every day.

points.label: Future for plans
points.text: She will walk to school tomorrow.

slides.inSimpleWords: Different tenses tell different types of information.

slides.title: Mixed Tenses in Dialogue
slides.storyContext: Priya practices: 'Yesterday I played (past). Today I play (present). Tomorrow I will play (future) cricket with my friend.'

example.problem: Write three tenses for 'sing'
example.solution: Past: sang. Present: sing. Future: will sing.

slides.inSimpleWords: Use all three tenses to tell complete stories.

slides.title: Complete the Tense Sentences
slides.storyContext: Arjun fills blanks: 'Last week I __ (go). This week I __ (go). Next week I __ (go) to the park.'

points.label: Answer
points.text: Past: went. Present: go. Future: will go.

slides.inSimpleWords: Practice all three tenses together.

slides.title: Present Progressive: Happening RIGHT NOW
slides.storyContext: Priya shows: 'I am reading. She is singing. They are playing.' This is RIGHT NOW in progress!

points.label: Form
points.text: am/is/are + verb-ing

points.label: Examples
points.text: I am eating. She is dancing. They are studying.

slides.inSimpleWords: Present progressive shows actions happening now.

slides.title: Present Progressive in Sentences
slides.storyContext: Arjun sees: 'The bird is flying. I am writing. We are laughing together right now!'

example.problem: Change to present progressive: 'I eat. She sings. They play.'
example.solution: I am eating. She is singing. They are playing.

slides.inSimpleWords: Add -ing and am/is/are for current action.

slides.title: Past Progressive: Was Happening Then
slides.storyContext: Priya explains: 'While I was reading, she was eating. They were playing outside when it rained.'

points.label: Form
points.text: was/were + verb-ing

points.label: Examples
points.text: I was eating. She was dancing. They were studying.

slides.inSimpleWords: Past progressive: action in progress in the past.

slides.title: Comparing All Tenses
slides.storyContext: Arjun summarizes: 'I ate (finished). I am eating (now). I will eat (future). I was eating (past moment). I have been eating (just started and continuing).'

example.problem: Write four tenses of 'play': simple, progressive (past and present), and future
example.solution: Played (past), was playing (past prog), play (present), am playing (present prog), will play (future)

slides.inSimpleWords: Mix progressive and simple tenses for nuance.

slides.title: Identify Tense Types in Paragraphs
slides.storyContext: Priya reads: 'Yesterday I played soccer. While I was playing, my friend arrived. Today I play chess. Tomorrow I will play cricket.'

points.label: Find tenses
points.text: played (simple past), was playing (past prog), play (simple present), will play (simple future)

slides.inSimpleWords: Spot different tense types in context.

slides.title: The Time Machine's Secret
slides.storyContext: The device shows: all three times matter. Your past shapes who you are. Your present is your power. Your future waits.
slides.inSimpleWords: Tenses help us tell complete stories.

image.alt: The Time Machine's Secret — Tenses

slides.title: Master Tenses Today
slides.storyContext: Past (walked), Present (walk), Future (will walk). Three gears of time.
slides.inSimpleWords: Tenses show when things happen.

image.alt: Master Tenses Today — Tenses

subject: English
title: Arjun and Priya Find the Magic Three
hook: A, an, the—three tiny words with big jobs. Discover when to use each one!

slides.title: Arjun and Priya Find the Magic Three
Three Mysterious Words
slides.storyContext: Arjun finds three old coins: 'a', 'an', and 'the'. Priya says, 'These aren't coins—they're magic words!'
slides.inSimpleWords: Three small words do big jobs.

image.alt: Three Mysterious Words — Articles

slides.title: What Are Articles?
slides.storyContext: Priya explains: 'Articles are tiny words that come before nouns. They tell if a noun is general or specific.'

points.label: What is an article?
points.text: A word that comes before a noun to show if it's general or specific

points.label: Three articles
points.text: A, An (indefinite), The (definite)

slides.inSimpleWords: Articles are words that come before nouns.

slides.title: The Indefinite Article: A
slides.storyContext: Priya holds one coin. 'Use A for nouns starting with consonants. A dog. A book. A school. It means one, not special.'

points.label: What does A do?
points.text: Introduces a general, non-specific noun (consonant sounds)

points.label: Examples
points.text: a dog, a ball, a pen, a house

slides.inSimpleWords: A: use before consonant sounds.

image.alt: The Indefinite Article: A — Articles

slides.title: Using 'A' in Sentences
slides.storyContext: Arjun writes: 'I have a cat. I see a tree. I eat a mango. I need a pencil.'

example.problem: Fill with 'a': '__ car, __ stone, __ river, __ toy'
example.solution: a car, a stone, a river, a toy

slides.inSimpleWords: 'A' introduces general, one-of-many things.

slides.title: The Indefinite Article: An
slides.storyContext: The second coin glows. 'An is for vowels. An apple. An elephant. An ice cream. Different sound, different article!'

points.label: What does An do?
points.text: Introduces a general noun (vowel sounds)

points.label: Examples
points.text: an apple, an elephant, an orange, an idea

slides.inSimpleWords: An: use before vowel sounds.

image.alt: The Indefinite Article: An — Articles

slides.title: Using 'An' in Sentences
slides.storyContext: Priya reads: 'I ate an apple. I saw an elephant. I have an idea. I need an eraser.'

example.problem: Fill with 'an': '__ egg, __ ant, __ umbrella, __ answer'
example.solution: an egg, an ant, an umbrella, an answer

slides.inSimpleWords: 'An' is for vowel-starting words.

slides.title: The Definite Article: The
slides.storyContext: The third coin is brightest. 'The is for specific things you know about. THE dog in our house. THE book on the table.'

points.label: What does The do?
points.text: Points to a specific, known noun

points.label: Examples
points.text: the dog, the sun, the school, the teacher

slides.inSimpleWords: The: use for known, specific things.

image.alt: The Definite Article: The — Articles

slides.title: Using 'The' in Sentences
slides.storyContext: Arjun points: 'I live in the city. I go to the school. The sun is bright. The moon is high.'

example.problem: Fill with 'the': '__ dog, __ river, __ stars, __ teacher'
example.solution: the dog, the river, the stars, the teacher (specific ones we know about)

slides.inSimpleWords: 'The' refers to specific things.

slides.title: A vs An: The Vowel Sound Rule
slides.storyContext: Priya explains: 'A before CONSONANT sounds. An before VOWEL sounds. Not the letter—the SOUND!'

points.label: Key rule
points.text: A/An depends on sound, not spelling

points.label: Examples
points.text: a university (yoo sound), an hour (silent h)

slides.inSimpleWords: Listen for the sound, not the letter.

slides.title: Articles in Sentences
slides.storyContext: Arjun reads: 'I have a cat. The cat is orange. An orange cat is cute.' Three articles, three jobs!

example.problem: When do I choose a, an, or the?
example.solution: a/an = general things. the = specific things you know.

slides.inSimpleWords: Match articles to each noun type.

image.alt: Articles in Sentences — Articles

slides.title: Complete Article Story
slides.storyContext: Priya writes: 'I saw a dog in the park. An old man fed the dog an apple.'

example.problem: Identify all articles and explain why: 'A girl found an old book in the library.'
example.solution: A (new/first girl), an (old starts with vowel sound), the (specific library)

slides.inSimpleWords: Every article choice tells a story.

slides.title: Fill the Articles
slides.storyContext: Priya gives Arjun blanks: '__ apple is red. __ dog barks at __ tree. __ sun is bright.' Choose a, an, or the!

points.label: Answer
points.text: An apple. A dog barks at the tree. The sun.

slides.inSimpleWords: Practice choosing the right article.

image.alt: Fill the Articles — Articles

slides.title: Article Detective
slides.storyContext: Arjun reads: 'Yesterday I bought __ bag. __ bag is blue. I put __ apple in __ bag.'

points.label: Challenge
points.text: I bought a bag. The bag is blue. I put an apple in the bag.

slides.inSimpleWords: Learn when each article fits best.

slides.title: Articles With Unique vs General Things
slides.storyContext: Priya explains: 'There's only ONE sun and ONE moon, so we always say THE sun, THE moon. But many cats, so A cat or THE cat (the one you mean).'

points.label: Unique things
points.text: Always use 'the': the sun, the moon, the Earth

points.label: General things
points.text: Use 'a' or 'an' first time, 'the' when mentioned again

slides.inSimpleWords: Unique things always get 'the'.

slides.title: Articles With First and Second Mention
slides.storyContext: Arjun writes: 'I saw a cat yesterday. The cat was orange. Today I saw a dog. The dog was brown.'

example.problem: Fill articles: 'There is __ tree in __ park. __ tree is old. __ birds live in __ tree.'
example.solution: There is a tree in the park. The tree is old. The birds live in the tree.

slides.inSimpleWords: First mention: 'a/an'. Later mentions: 'the'.

slides.title: No Article With Plural and Uncountable Nouns
slides.storyContext: Priya teaches: 'Some words don't need articles. 'Cats are cute' (plural). 'I like milk' (uncountable). 'I like sports' (general plural).'

points.label: Plural nouns
points.text: Cats are here (no article needed for general plurals)

points.label: Uncountable
points.text: Water is important (no article for general amounts)

slides.inSimpleWords: Some nouns don't need articles at all.

slides.title: When Articles Aren't Needed
slides.storyContext: Arjun notices: 'I like apples (not 'a apples' or 'the apples' for general). Milk is good (not 'a milk' or 'the milk').'

example.problem: Do these need articles? 'I love __ sports. __ Dogs are friendly. __ Water helps plants grow.'
example.solution: No articles needed for general statements with plurals or uncountables. Just: I love sports. Dogs are friendly. Water helps plants grow.

slides.inSimpleWords: Generalized plurals skip articles.

slides.title: Full Article Practice
slides.storyContext: Priya gives Arjun: 'Fill ALL articles: '__ boy went to __ store. He bought __ red shirt and __ blue pants. __ Shirt is __ gift for __ friend.'

points.label: Answer
points.text: A boy went to the store. He bought a red shirt and blue pants. The shirt is a gift for a friend.

slides.inSimpleWords: Practice all article rules together.

slides.title: Articles With Adjectives
slides.storyContext: Arjun writes: 'A big house. The big house. An old toy. The old toy.' Adjectives come BETWEEN articles and nouns!

points.label: Pattern
points.text: Article + adjective + noun (a big cat, the small dog)

points.label: Multiple adjectives
points.text: a bright red ball, the tall dark tree

slides.inSimpleWords: Articles come before adjectives.

slides.title: Complex Articles with Adjectives
slides.storyContext: Priya writes: 'I saw an amazing red butterfly. An intelligent young student won the prize.'

example.problem: Fill articles and check word order: '__ beautiful garden with __ colorful flowers'
example.solution: A beautiful garden with colorful flowers (or: The beautiful garden with the colorful flowers)

slides.inSimpleWords: Articles + adjectives + nouns make rich descriptions.

slides.title: Articles vs Possessives
slides.storyContext: Arjun learns: 'The book (not mine, just any book). My book (MY copy). Her book (HER copy). Use articles OR possessives, not both!'

points.label: Articles
points.text: a, an, the (no possession shown)

points.label: Possessives
points.text: my, your, his, her, its, our, their (ownership clear)

slides.inSimpleWords: Don't mix 'the' with 'my' or 'his'.

slides.title: Article vs Possessive Choices
slides.storyContext: Priya corrects: 'Not 'the my book' — say 'my book' OR 'the book'. Pick one!

example.problem: Correct: 'I like the her dog' and 'I saw a their house'
example.solution: I like her dog (use possessive). I saw their house (use possessive). OR: I like the dog that belongs to her. I saw the house that belongs to them.

slides.inSimpleWords: Choose articles OR possessives, not both.

slides.title: Mix Articles, Adjectives, and Possessives
slides.storyContext: Arjun builds: 'My old book is on the table. An interesting story is in the book. His new pen works well.'

points.label: Challenge
points.text: Write using articles + adjectives OR possessives correctly in 3 sentences

slides.inSimpleWords: Combine all article rules in real sentences.

slides.title: The Coins Unite
slides.storyContext: The three coins merge. Arjun realizes: a, an, and the are partners. Together they help sentences sound perfect.
slides.inSimpleWords: Articles are glue for good English.

image.alt: The Coins Unite — Articles

slides.title: Master These Three
slides.storyContext: A (consonants), An (vowels), The (specific). Use them every day!
slides.inSimpleWords: Three articles unlock clear writing.
